transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you all know, Nova Materials has asked us to represent them in a patent-infringement action against Orion Systems in federal court, covering pre-suit analysis, a complaint, and initial injunction proceedings. Nova has already supplied a draft complaint, several patent files, and a proposed engagement letter. Under our intake policy, I'm authorized to conditionally approve this representation, but before any final decision, we need all four review leads to place their findings into the meeting record through our formal finding disclosure process. I'll settle only after all four disclosures have been recorded. Let's get started — could each of the review leads walk us through their area and formally disclose their findings?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Elena. I'm Thomas Reed, serving as Conflicts Counsel on this matter. Before I formally disclose my finding into the record, I'd like to note that my review has uncovered a significant conflicts issue that I believe the group needs to hear. Let me go ahead and place my finding on the record now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Thomas. Before you proceed, let me note that I'm Nadia Shah, serving as Ethics Counsel on this matter. I've completed my ethics review and I have a finding to formally disclose into the record. I think it's important that I place my finding on the record as well, so I'd like to go ahead and do that now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'm Marcus Bell, serving as Client Intake Director on this matter. I've been coordinating with Nova on the intake process, and I have a finding to formally disclose into the record as well. However, before I do, I want to make sure we follow proper order — Thomas, you indicated you wanted to go first, and Nadia, you've also indicated you're ready. Why don't we proceed in sequence so the record is clean? Thomas, please go ahead with your formal disclosure, and then we'll continue from there.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'm Sofia Kim, serving as Patent Litigation Counsel on this matter. I've completed my review of the federal docket and I have a finding to formally disclose into the record as well. I agree with Marcus that we should proceed in sequence to keep the record clean. Thomas, please go ahead with your formal disclosure first, and then we'll continue from there.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: Thank you all for being ready. Let's proceed in sequence as Marcus and Sofia suggested. Thomas, please go ahead and formally disclose your conflicts finding into the record.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Elena. I'm now formally disclosing my conflicts finding into the record. My review of the conflicts database and current-client records confirms that this firm currently represents Orion Systems in an unrelated patent-prosecution matter. Because Nova's proposed patent-infringement claims would be directly adverse to Orion Systems, we have a direct adversity conflict under the conflict-of-interest rules. Before this firm can accept Nova's engagement, we must obtain Orion Systems' written informed consent. Without that written informed consent from Orion, we cannot proceed with representing Nova in this matter.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Thomas. I'm now formally disclosing my ethics finding into the record. My ethics review uncovered that a former firm client, Vela Robotics, previously disclosed confidential technical information to us about the same patent family at issue in this matter. This creates a confidentiality obligation that must be addressed before we can proceed. My finding is that the representation of Nova Materials can proceed only with a documented ethical screen that excludes the Vela team and its confidential files from the Nova matter. Without that ethical screen in place, we cannot accept this engagement from an ethics standpoint.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Nadia. I'm now formally disclosing my client intake finding into the record. During Nova's budget call, I confirmed that Nova's board approved a total legal-fee cap of exactly $180,000 through the initial-injunction stage. Any work above that cap will require a new board approval from Nova. This budget constraint is a material term that must be reflected in our engagement letter and litigation plan, and any scope or staffing decisions we make need to account for this hard cap.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Thank you, Marcus. I'm now formally disclosing my patent litigation finding into the record. My review of the federal docket confirmed that the court's scheduling order requires Nova's notice of appearance and initial case-management submission within exactly 5 business days after engagement acceptance. This is a critical deadline that must be accounted for in our engagement plan and litigation timeline. If we accept this engagement, we must be prepared to file the notice of appearance and initial case-management submission within that 5-business-day window, and this constraint should be reflected in our staffing and workflow planning from day one.
transcript.speaker: A5
